name: LangChain, Inc.
subcategory: LLM application / agent frameworks plus agent observability, evaluation and deployment platform (LangSmith)
origin_detail: Launched in October 2022 as an open-source side project by Harrison Chase while he worked at ML startup Robust Intelligence (GitHub repo created 2022-10-17); company founded in early 2023 by Chase and Ankush Gola; HQ San Francisco with offices in New York, Boston and Amsterdam
flagship_projects: LangSmith (proprietary platform: observability, evaluation, deployment/Agent Server, Fleet, gateways)
openness_notes: Initial 3: from Oct 2022 until LangSmith, the whole product was the MIT-licensed LangChain library and the company sold nothing proprietary. Current 2 (open core): the frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, deepagents) remain MIT, but the revenue product is LangSmith, launched Feb 2024 as a closed-source observability and evaluation platform and since extended to deployment (LangGraph Platform, GA 2025-05-14, later folded into LangSmith as Deployment/Agent Server), Agent Builder, Fleet, LLM and tool gateways and fine-tuning; it is sold per seat ($0 Developer, $39/seat Plus, custom Enterprise) plus metered usage, with self-hosted and hybrid deployment only on Enterprise. LangSmith is explicitly framework-agnostic. No relicensing: the framework licence has been MIT throughout; a 2023-11-29 commit only changed the copyright holder from Harrison Chase to LangChain Inc.

license_history.note: Commit #13300 (2023-11-29) changed copyright from @hwchase17 to LangChain Inc.; licence type unchanged
LangSmith launched Feb 2024 as a closed-source observability and evaluation platform

license_history.license: Proprietary managed service (LangGraph Platform, later LangSmith Deployment)
license_history.note: GA 2025-05-14; by Oct 2025 renamed Deployment within LangSmith
LangChain 1.0 released 2025-10-22; legacy code moved to langchain-classic

risk_events: Jul 2025: TechCrunch sources put ARR at only $12-16M, three months before a $1.25B valuation (Oct 2025) and 16 months before a $3B valuation (Nov 2026)
Monetisation depends on LangSmith, a separate closed product; the MIT frameworks can be used, forked or replaced without paying
API churn: LangChain 1.0 (Oct 2025) moved legacy functionality into a separate langchain-classic package
Single-vendor governance: no foundation for LangChain or LangGraph
robustness: Very large open footprint: langchain had ~150k GitHub stars and 25k forks (Nov 2026), langgraph ~45k stars, langchain + langgraph had 90M combined monthly downloads (Oct 2025) and LangChain reports more than 1B cumulative open-source downloads. MIT code would survive the company. The commercial side has >7,000 organisations on LangSmith (Nov 2026), 35% of the Fortune 500, and $460M raised, the last $300M in Nov 2026.
physical_science_relevance: Indirect: a general-purpose agent and RAG framework that research groups can use to build literature, data or lab-tool agents; no science-specific product found on fetched pages.
openness_effect_assessment: The permissive framework gave LangChain a huge funnel (118k stars by Oct 2025, ~150k by Nov 2026, 1B+ downloads) and the company monetised it through a separate closed platform rather than by relicensing. Reported revenue was small relative to adoption ($12-16M ARR in mid-2025), yet valuations rose from a reported $200M (2023) to $1.25B (Oct 2025) and $3B (Nov 2026), so investors priced the distribution the open framework created and the agent-platform position, not current licence revenue.
key_takeaway: LangChain is the AI-era template of a permissive framework plus a proprietary SaaS: MIT from day one with no relicensing, the paid product (LangSmith) kept outside the open repo from launch and made framework-agnostic, and $460M raised at a $3B valuation (2026-11-13). It shows open source still works as a go-to-market in the AI era when the business is a hosted, closed companion product rather than the open code itself.
